protocols.script: Your honor, this is the interpreter speaking. The interpreter requires a comfort break. May the interpreter be excused for a brief comfort break?
notes: Need a bathroom break during long hearing

protocols.script: Your honor, interpreter has been advised by LSU that only consecutive interpretation is permitted on WebEx. Currently, calling in and connecting to WebEx at the same time is not allowed.
notes: Judge is asking for SIM: Please take down the judge’s name and advise management if judge insists

protocols.script: Your honor, this is the interpreter speaking. I would be glad to adjust my sound settings. Please allow a brief moment as I make adjustments.
notes: Judge complains about background noise (Message through WebEx if judge cannot hear you.)
1. Adjust AUDIO INPUT settings on WebEx
2. Signal collegues you are in a call having audio issues

protocols.situation: Computer loses connection to mic and headset
protocols.script: Your honor, this is the interpreter speaking. Interpreter needs to restart workstation due to technical issues. Please allow a brief moment while the computer restarts, interpreter will reconnect shortly. Thank you for your patience.

(if judge can't hear you, message through WebEx)
advised that you are restarting you PC and will

protocols.situation: Asked 'Are you in a Call Center', 'Where are you?'
protocols.script: No, your honor, interpreter is in a private desk in an office shared with other interpreters.

Your honor, interpreter requires repetition, May interpreter request the respondant for repetition?' -or- 'Your honor, interpreter requires repetition. May interpreter request repetition of your last sentence(s)/phrase(s).'
Your honor, interpreter requires clarification. May interpreter request clarification from the respondant?' -or- 'Your honor, interpreter requires clarification, with the term XYZ, do you mean XYZ?'

protocols.situation: Ask to look up a term
protocols.script: 'Your honor, the interpreter requires a moment to look up a term' -or- 'This is the interpreter speaking. May the interpeter be allowed a brief moment to verify the definition of a term?'

protocols.situation: Judge won't allow you to adjust your audio settings
protocols.script: Your honor, interpreter requires adjustment of audio settings. May interpreter be allowed a moment for adjustment of audio settings? This is imperative for interpreter to provide an accurate rendition of this session.
notes: If judge gets annoyed and seems to be agitated to the point of a possible complaint, please offer reassigning the order to another interpreter and move to (reassignment of hearing protocol).

protocols.situation: Scheduled for attachment with same judge
protocols.script: Your honor, interpreter is set to connect with you in two hours for COI 9876543. May you please confirm our recconection time and time zone for that hearing after this session?

protocols.situation: Cannot hear one (or more) of the call participants, but can hear the others
protocols.script: 'Your honor, the audio from (Mr./MS XYZ) is inaudible. May the interpreter ask (Mr./MS XYZ) to get closer to thier microphone or adjust their headset? ' -or- 'Your honor, when you speak the the audio is inaudible. May interpreter kindly ask you to face your microphone/get closer to your micophone?'
Interpreter stands by his/her interpretation' -or- 'Interpreter made a mistake and would like to correct it. (Fill in correct interpretation/rendition)'
notes: Please remember that interpreters, as professionals may politely correct their interpretation. Do NOT apologize: It is important to make a smooth correction and continue with confidence than to apologize and lose credibiity.

protocols.situation: Reassignment of hearing for emergency, technical issue
protocols.script: Your honor, this is the interpreter speaking. Interpreter will have to leave for an unforeseen situation, please excuse interpreter. Another interpreter will join shortly as the case gets reassigned. Thank you and sorry for any inconvenience.
notes: 1. If your outside-of-work emergency or appointment is coming up, or 2. You are having time consuming technical issues please advise our scheduling team ASAP. Be mindful that reassigning an order may only be done by coordinators and may take up to 15 minutes to complete. The court needs to be advised for this to take place properly. Also please wait for replacement interpreter to connect before disconnecting.

protocols.script: Your honor, it has been a pleasure to serve in this call. Will you need interpreter to reconnect for a later hearing? -or- Interpreter (your name here) disconnecting. Thank you for using our service.
notes: 1. Ask if the court will need you for additional
2. Proper words to end the call (say goodbye)

protocols.script: Your Honor, the interpreter cannot proceed without clarificaion/repetition as this will impede my ability to deliver my services.
notes: Interpreters should keep in mind that excessive requests for clarification/repetition almost always raise concerns with IJs, and if there is an impediment to their clearly hearing or understanding the hearing parties that causes requests for clarification/repetition, it's advisable that such impediment is escalated to the IJ so the court is not under the impression that the issue is with the interpreter.

protocolNotes.title: Remaining in Conduit
protocolNotes.body: An interpreter should always STAY IN CONDUIT which means that he/she always speaks in third party tense. Interpreters are an (invisible wall of language) and should only render what either party says in the opposite language. Therefore, to speak for yourself ALWAYS introduce yourself into the conversation as "This is the interpreter speaking"

protocolNotes.title: Addressing your customer
protocolNotes.body: Interpreters should always address your customer, in our case THE JUDGE, so if you need for any reason to refer to the respondent, attorney or have any issue. Remember to use the "This is the interpreter speaking" then address the judge for any issue not covered in our protocols

protocolNotes.title: Mistakes and corrections
protocolNotes.body: Interpreters should always maintain professionalism and confidence. If you at any point make a mistake and need to correct it. Don't apologize, but correct yourself as smoothly as possible then resume interpretation. If you have been corrected and you used the correct state (Interpreter stands by his/her interpretation). If correction is accurate, correct it and move on.

simTips: Leave a Term in Original Language is you can't transfer it
SIMPLIFY, rather than chase everything being said
Let respondant know you missed a part, and continue

disqualifications.title: Administrative
disqualifications.body: Leaving Webex VRI without official release by Judge Constant tardiness – arriving via Webex after the work order start time Arriving in the Webex room with insufficient time to setup; not being ready to perform services by the work order start time Talking to the court personnel (via WebEx) about work order details Requesting to leave early (e.g., needing login to another work order or leave early for the day) instead of contacting the SOSi Coordinator using all means of communication

disqualifications.title: Professionalism
disqualifications.body: Unprofessional behavior with court staff (e.g., arguing, placing demands via WebEx, refusing to interpret without being officially released by court staff) Lack of professional demeanor and attitude in the EOIR court via WebEx (e.g., making inappropriate comments about the judge’s ruling, advising the lawyers, inserting opinion) Lack of full understanding and adherence to the Immigration Court Guidelines for Contract Interpreters and the Contract Interpreter Code of Professional Responsibility

disqualifications.title: Performance
disqualifications.body: Inadequate interpreting skills; unable to provide full and complete interpretation which is required in all courts unless directed otherwise by the judge Inadequate understanding and use of immigration court and relevant judicial terminology Inability to effectively operate VRI equipment that is required for each hearing (e.g., laptop/desktop, headset with integrated microphone, high speed internet, working camera on device, professional workspace with SOSi background) Unable to keep up with the pace of the hearing (words per minute) Failure to disclose language dialect issues and/or a conflict of interest between the Respondent and the Interpreter as soon as known. Failure to request repetitions, clarifications, etc., when needed, or use of improper request protocol.

scripts.en: Pending before this court is also the respondent's request to depart the United States without expense to the Government in lieu of removal under section 240B(b) of the Act. To qualify for voluntary departure, the respondent must establish that he has been physically present in the United States for a period of at least one year immediately preceding the date the NTA was served; he is, and has been a person of good moral character for at least 5 years immediately preceding such application; he is not deportable under section 237(a)(2)(A)(iii) or 237(a)(4) of the Act; he establishes by clear and convincing evidence that he has the means to depart the United States and intends to do so; and he shall be required to post a voluntary departure bond. In addition, the respondent must be in possession of a travel document that will assure his lawful reentry into his home country. Discretionary consideration of an application for voluntary departure involves a weighing of factors, including the respondent's prior immigration history, the length of his residence in the United States, and the extent of his family, business and societal ties in the United States. There are no other issues raised by the DHS that will further negatively affect the respondent's eligibility for this minimal form of relief. The Court finds the respondent statutorily eligible and deserving of this relief in the exercise of discretion. Accordingly, the following order(s) are entered: IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that the respondent’s application for asylum be denied. IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the respondent be removed from the United States to El Salvador, or in the alternative to Mexico, on the charges contained in the Notice to Appear. IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the respondent’s application for withholding of removal under section 241(b)(3) of the Act to El Salvador be denied. IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the respondent be granted voluntary departure, in lieu of removal, and without expense to the United States Government on or before May 15th, 2014. IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the respondent shall post a voluntary departure bond in the amount of $ 5,000 with the Department of Homeland Security on or before March 20th, 2014 IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that, if required by the DHS, the respondent shall present to the DHS all necessary travel documents for voluntary departure within 60 days. IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that, if the respondent fails to comply with any of the above orders, the voluntary departure order shall without further notice or proceedings vacate the next day, and the respondent shall be removed from the United States to El Salvador on the charges contained in the Notice to Appear. WARNING TO THE RESPONDENT: Failure to depart as required means you could be removed from the United States, you may have to pay a civil penalty of $1000 to $5000, and you would become ineligible for voluntary departure, cancellation of removal, and any change or adjustment of status for 10 years to come. Also, if you fail to depart as required, and then fail to comply with the removal order, you could also be fined $500 for each day of noncompliance. Section 274D of the Act (for 212 and 237). In addition, if you are removable for being deportable under section 237 of the Act, and you fail to comply with your removal order, you shall face additional fines and/or could be imprisoned for up to 4 and in some cases up to 10 years.
scripts.es: Pendiente ante este juzgado también está la solicitud del compareciente para salir de los Estados Unidos sin costo para el gobierno en lugar de expulsión en virtud del artículo 240B(b) de la ley. Para calificar para salida voluntaria, el compareciente debe establecer que ha estado físicamente presente en los Estados Unidos por un periodo de por lo menos 1 año inmediatamente presidiendo la fecha en la que el Aviso de Comparecencia fue entregado; es; y ha sido una persona de buena solvencia moral por lo menos 5 años precediendo inmediatamente esa solicitud; no es sujeto a deportación bajo el Artículo 237(a)(2)(A)(iii)o 237(a)(4) de la ley; establece por evidencia clara y convincente que cuenta con los medios para salir de los Estados Unidos y tiene la intención de hacerlo; y requerirá pagar una fianza de salida voluntaria. Adicionalmente, el compareciente debe contar con un documento que asegure su ingreso legal a su país de origen. La consideración discrecional de una solicitud de Salida Voluntaria envuelve sopesar varios factores, incluyendo el historial migratorio del compareciente, su duración de residencia en los Estados Unidos, y el alcance de sus vínculos familiares, comerciales y sociales en los Estados Unidos. No hay otras cuestiones planteadas por parte de Gobernación que afecten negativamente los méritos del compareciente para este beneficio migratorio mínimo. En ejercicio de su discreción, el Tribunal considera que el compareciente reúne los requisitos legales y es merecedor de este beneficio. En consecuencia, se dictan las siguientes órdenes: SE ORDENA POR LA PRESENTE que la solicitud de asilo por parte del compareciente sea denegada. SE ORDENA ADEMÁS que el compareciente sea expulsado de Estados Unidos a El Salvador o, en su defecto, a México, por los cargos contenidos en el Aviso de Comparecencia. SE ORDENA ADEMÁS que se deniegue la solicitud de retención de la expulsión a El Salvador del compareciente en virtud del artículo 241(b)(3) de la Ley. SE ORDENA ADEMÁS que se conceda salida voluntaria en lugar de expulsión, al compareciente, y sin gastos para el Gobierno de Estados Unidos en o antes del 15 de mayo de 2014. SE ORDENA ADEMÁS que el compareciente deposite una fianza de salida voluntaria por un monto de 5.000 dólares con Gobernación en o antes del 20 de marzo de 2014. SE ORDENA ADEMÁS que, si así lo requiere Gobernación, el compareciente presente a Gobernación todos los documentos de viaje necesarios para salida voluntaria dentro de 60 días. SE ORDENA ADEMÁS que, si el compareciente incumple cualquiera de las órdenes anteriores, la orden de salida voluntaria quedará sin efecto al día siguiente, sin más aviso ni diligencias, y el compareciente será expulsado de los Estados Unidos a El Salvador por los cargos contenidos en el Aviso de Comparecencia. ADVERTENCIA AL COMPARECIENTE: Si no sale como se requiere, podría ser expulsado de los Estados Unidos, podría tener que pagar una multa civil de entre $1000 a $5000, y dejaría de ser apto para salida voluntaria, cancelación de expulsión, y cualquier cambio o ajuste de estatus durante 10 años. Además, si no sale como se le exige y luego incumple la orden de expulsión, también podría ser multado con 500 dólares por cada día de incumplimiento. Sección 274D de la Ley (para 212 y 237). Además, si es sujeto a expulsión por ser deportable en virtud del artículo 237 de la Ley, y no cumple la orden de expulsión, enfrentará multas adicionales y/o podría ser encarcelado hasta 4 años y, en algunos casos, hasta 10 años.

scripts.type: IC INITIAL HEARING - PRO SE INTRODUCTION P1
scripts.en: To the respondent through the interpreter, what language do you speak and understand best? [if not English] These proceedings will be interpreted today in the [name] language. This is an initial [removal] [deportation] [exclusion] hearing before Immigration Judge (Name of Judge) in (City, State) on [date], in the matter of [name], case number A [number]. APPEARANCES - The respondent is appearing pro se. Counsel for the government, please state your appearance for the record. The interpreter today is [name]. Can you hear the interpreter clearly through the headphones? Do you understand the interpreter? If at any time, you have difficulty understanding the interpreter, please let me know immediately. [if EOIR employee] [name] is the official interpreter for the Immigration Court who will be providing simultaneous interpretation into the [name] language, and need not be sworn in. [if not EOIR employee] To the interpreter, do you swear or affirm that you are competent to translate from English to [language] and from [language] to English, and that you will do so accurately and completely? To the Respondent, the Government asserts that you are in the US in violation of law. The purpose of the hearing is to determine whether you are an alien and, if so, if you are in the US in violation of law. The Court must determine whether there any provision of law that would permit you to remain in the US permanently and, if that if not possible, whether you will be leaving the US under an order of removal or an order of voluntary departure. These questions will be answered after hearing all of the facts of the case. OATH - To the respondent, Sir/Madam, would you be willing to swear an oath to tell the truth? Yes - please stand and raise your right hand. Do you swear that the testimony you will provide in these proceedings will be the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth? No - please stand and raise your right hand. Do you affirm that the testimony you will provide in these proceedings will be the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth? BIOGRAPHICS -Please state your full and true name for the record. Where do you currently live? Same - You are being provided with a blue change of address form. If you do move at any time during these proceedings, you must complete a change of address form and file it with the court within five days of moving. Do you understand? Different - Please complete two blue change of address forms and complete them at this time. Please provide one to the court clerk and the other to the government attorney. Please take an additional blue change of address form with you. If you move again at any time during these proceedings, you must complete a change of address form and file it with the court within five days of moving. Do you understand? SUMMARY-The purpose of these proceedings is to determine whether or not you should be allowed to remain in the United States. Do you understand? You have the right to be represented during these hearings by an attorney or qualified representative at your own expense. The government cannot provide you with an attorney or qualified representative. The court clerk is providing you with a legal aid list of individuals and organizations that may be able to represent you at little or no cost. Do you understand? Do you want more time to get a lawyer or representative to help you in these proceedings?

scripts.type: IC INITIAL HEARING - PRO SE INTRODUCTION P2
scripts.en: CONTINUE-Yes - Because you have stated that you want time to locate an attorney, I will continue your case to [date] at [time]. I encourage you to use the legal aid list. If the first organization cannot help you, please contact the second organization until you find one that can help you. Do you understand? If you cannot find or afford an attorney or organization to represent you, be prepared to speak for yourself at the next hearing. Do you understand? I want to warn you that you may encounter unscrupulous individuals, in fact, some may be outside in the halls of this building, that present themselves as notarios that can help you in these proceedings. These individuals are not attorneys, and they may not represent you in this court. If a person says that he or she can represent you and you are not certain that they are an attorney, ask to see proof that they can represent you in this court. If someone agrees to represent you in these proceedings, be sure to get that person’s business card. If you pay that person any money to assist you in these proceedings, be sure to get a receipt for any money you have paid. Finally, you should get a written description of what that person will do for you during the course of their representation. Do you understand everything I have said to you? WAIVER OF RIGHT TO COUNSEL-No - Does that mean that you want to do your immigration case yourself right now? Yes - Because you have stated that you do not wish to continue this hearing to try to find an attorney, do you understand that you will be required to represent yourself in these proceedings? Do you understand that you will be required to plead to the allegations and charge of law contained in the Notice to Appear? Do you understand that the decisions you make here today may affect the outcome of your case? Do you acknowledge that you are making this decision of your own free will, and that you have not been coerced in anyway to forego your right to representation? Do you still want to proceed today, without the assistance of an attorney or qualified representative, and represent yourself in this hearing? I find that the respondent’s waiver of his right to an attorney has been given knowingly and voluntarily, and the court will proceed with this hearing. [PROCEED TO CONTINUED HEARING SCRIPT - PRO SE] NOTICE AND RIGHTS The clerk is providing you with the only written notice you will receive of the next hearing. The clerk is also providing you with an advisal of your rights. You must return here on [date] at [time]. Please arrive early. If you do not appear at the next hearing as ordered you will be ordered deported and removed from the United States, unless you can show that your absence was caused by exceptional circumstances beyond your control. Exceptional circumstances are defined as a serious illness or death of an immediate family member. If you are ordered removed, any applications for relief you may have pending before this court will be deemed abandoned and will be denied. Additionally, you will become ineligible for certain forms of relief, such as voluntary departure, cancellation of removal, adjustment of status, or change of status for a period of ten years. Do you understand everything I have said to you today? Do you have any questions about anything I have told you today? Anything from the government? There being nothing further, this matter is continued to the date and time indicated on the notice provided to the parties. Thank you.
